grapefruit.name: Grapefruit

sections.whatItOffers: Half a pink or red grapefruit gives about half the daily vitamin C reference and some vitamin A, for around 50 calories. It is tart and juicy, with a pleasantly bitter edge.
sections.practicalServing: ½ grapefruit (USDA: 0.5 fruit, 3¾ in across = 123 g)
sections.howToEatIt: Eat in segments with a spoon, add to salads with avocado or fennel, or grill with a little cinnamon.
sections.cycleRelevance: Vitamin C helps your body absorb plant iron from the same meal (NIH ODS), so a piece of grapefruit alongside beans, lentils or greens is a useful pairing. No phase-specific claim is made.

source.usdaDescription: Grapefruit, raw, pink and red, all areas
source.portion: ½ grapefruit (USDA: 0.5 fruit, 3¾ in across = 123 g)

grapes.name: Grapes

sections.whatItOffers: Grapes are sweet, easy-to-eat fruit with some potassium and vitamin K. A cup is mostly water and natural sugars.
sections.howToEatIt: Eat them as they are, chilled or frozen, or add halved grapes to chicken or grain salads and cheese boards.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for grapes.

kiwi.name: Kiwi

sections.whatItOffers: One kiwifruit supplies about 85% of the daily vitamin C reference, along with potassium, vitamin K and a little vitamin E and fibre.
sections.howToEatIt: Halve and scoop with a spoon, slice into yoghurt or salads, or blend into smoothies. The skin is edible if washed, though many people peel it.
sections.cycleRelevance: Vitamin C helps your body absorb plant iron from the same meal (NIH ODS), so a piece of kiwi alongside beans, lentils or greens is a useful pairing. No phase-specific claim is made.

papaya.name: Papaya

sections.whatItOffers: Papaya is a soft, sweet tropical fruit that is an excellent source of vitamin C (about 118% of the reference in a cup) with folate and potassium.
sections.howToEatIt: Scoop ripe papaya with lime juice, cube it into fruit salads and salsas, or blend it into smoothies.
sections.cycleRelevance: Folate is a nutrient some women of childbearing age do not get enough of (NIH ODS), and a cup of papaya provides about 13% of the reference. No phase-specific claim is made.
